target.title: fix(android): parse string booleans in talk gateway config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`TalkModeGatewayConfigParser` only accepted strict JSON boolean literals for `interruptOnSpeech` (`true`/`false` via `booleanOrNull`). Gateway configs that serialize booleans as strings — for example `"interruptOnSpeech": "true"` — were silently ignored, so Talk mode never enabled interrupt-on-speech even when the operator configured it.

This is inconsistent with sibling Android parsers that already accept string booleans:
- `TalkDirectiveParser.asBooleanOrNull()` accepts `"true"`, `"false"`, `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"1"`, `"0"`
- `GatewaySession` JSON helpers use the same pattern

## Why This Change Was Made

Align talk gateway config parsing with the existing string-boolean convention used elsewhere in the Android app. The fix is localized to `TalkModeGatewayConfig.kt` and does not change silence-timeout parsing (which intentionally rejects string numerics).

## User Impact

Operators whose gateway config emits string booleans for talk settings will see `interruptOnSpeech` honored in Talk mode instead of falling back to default behavior.

## Evidence

**Regression test:** `TalkModeConfigParsingTest.parsesStringInterruptOnSpeechFlag`

Input:
```json
{ "talk": { "interruptOnSpeech": "true" } }
```

Expected: `TalkModeGatewayConfigParser.parse(config).interruptOnSpeech == true`

**Proof command:**
```bash
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeConfigParsingTest
```

**Changed files:**
- `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeGatewayConfig.kt`
- `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeConfigParsingTest.kt`
